beats.t: Spring, three years later. Yeoni woke ten minutes before the alarm. The radio reported that cherry blossoms had begun opening outside.
A photograph clung to the refrigerator door. The seaside. Two umbrellas. A lunch box of split-open gimbap. Four people, all caught with their eyes closed.
Not one decent shot. Giving him the selfie stick was a mistake.
A cushion still rested at the foot of the bed. Habit now. Today, a white dress hung beside it.
It's really today. Not a dream, right?
[ App notification · Park Byeongha: Awake? Match your socks. Today, seriously. ]
First text on our wedding morning is socks? What about 'I love you'?
Yeoni wrote a reply, deleted it, and wrote again. Matched. Photo attached. Two matching white socks.
[ Park Byeongha: Passed. ]
He really hasn't changed.
Yeoni took the old notebook from a drawer. The sentence on its last page remained: Even in a different form, Neo. On my side.
Below it, they wrote today's date and added one line: Now my husband. Then slipped the notebook into the dress bag's inner pocket.
The doorbell rang. Before Yeoni could open it, elegant, polite speech reached them. Cool at the endings, yet strangely warm.
Bride, I've brought your makeup artist. And umbrellas. Rain is forecast this afternoon.
Rain? On my wedding day?
Don't worry. April rain passes quickly. And rainy weddings mean a happy marriage. Saebyeok said so.
We agreed to believe only half of what Saebyeok says.
The problem is that half is usually right.
Seo Hanbi now managed the convenience store. The woman who had worked nights to repay umbrellas had taken over when the owner retired. The world accepted strange people better than expected.
Her notebook still stayed in her bag. Every line had a circle. Except the very last.
[ And Yeoni ]
Still leaving that line unchecked?
Yes. I thought I'd circle it today. A wedding gift.
Don't. Leave it open forever. Come as a friend, not to repay me.
Seo Hanbi looked at the notebook for a long time, then put her pen back. Instead of a circle, she had drawn a tiny umbrella at the line's end.
Then this. A mark of sharing, not repayment.
After makeup, Seo Hanbi fastened the dress buttons one by one with careful fingers. In the mirror, she briefly lowered her eyes.
The Yeoni of the first spring wanted a dress like this too. We talked about it at the bus stop.
What did that spring's me say?
That you hoped it would rain on your wedding day. An excuse to share an umbrella.
That spring's me was very me.
I can't repay that Yeoni. So I'll be twice as good to this spring's Yeoni.
Forget twice as good. Just catch the bouquet today. I'll aim at you.
The venue was the riverside park behind the university. Kang Saebyeok stood in a suit before the front row, an emcee script in his hand and a perpetual calendar in his pocket.
One check before the bride enters. I haven't received today's auspicious-date selection fee.
Deduct it from your wedding gift.
Then I have to give a larger gift. Strange arithmetic.
Saebyeok now ran a small consultation office instead of a campus tent. The sign still read: Birth time unknown? I'll work it out.
Behind him sat a small middle-aged woman. She waved when she met Yeoni's eyes. Saebyeok reddened to the tips of his ears.
My mother. She came along. Wanted to see the people who call her son's name.
Ma'am! Do you know Saebyeok scams people with compatibility readings?
That was a secret!
Laughing, the woman called her son. Saebyeok. Instead of answering, he opened his script. Upside down.
And a congratulatory message has arrived. From very far away.
[ App notification · Moka: I'm rapping the wedding song. Dodam on drums, Museong on chorus. No refusals. I'm a five-star performer. ]
Can't refuse this one.
Whether the rap plays in this world, I don't know. The universe will handle it.
A drum really sounded from the phone speaker. Clumsy and joyous. Above it came a boy's clear voice, then rap drowning that voice out.
Still off-key.
That's the charm. Nobody's mocking him.
A short aisle beneath cherry trees. At its end stood Park Byeongha. The white strand of hair remained. His tie was slightly crooked.
Yeoni walked alone, without taking their father's arm. They had insisted. This path, at least, they wanted to walk on their own feet.
Late.
Three minutes. Nothing compared with how long you waited.
True.
Laughter rose from the guests. Yeoni straightened Byeongha's tie. He stood still like a tamed cat.
Yeoni. In the first spring, we never made it this far.
I know. That's why I walked here this time. By myself.
Yes. On your own feet. I didn't drag you here.
Yeoni understood. A vine winds around Metal to climb, but Metal doesn't pull the vine upward. They simply support one another.
Now the vows. Groom first.
I'm not good with words, so I'll keep it short. But I'll keep it for a long time.
I'll match your socks. If you go out in mismatched ones, I won't get angry. Might scold a little.
That's a vow?
And I'll never hide my name while staying beside you again. From beginning to end, as Park Byeongha. As Neo.
The guests fell silent. Seo Hanbi took out a handkerchief. Saebyeok lowered his head, pretending to read his script.
My turn.
When it rains, I'll carry the yellow umbrella. Half for you, half for me. No complaints about wet shoulders.
I'll rate you again every year. Stars may come off. Stay alert.
Already nervous.
They joined hands. The center of Yeoni's palm warmed. Byeongha's hand was a little cold, then quickly matched its temperature. Eul and Gyeong. Vine and Metal.
Then rain truly began. Fine spring rain. Guests murmured. Seo Hanbi drew umbrellas from her bag: one yellow, one black.
See? Bought with my own money this time.
Yeoni opened the yellow umbrella and tilted half toward Byeongha. Their own shoulder grew wet. Silently, he pushed the shaft back toward Yeoni.
I said half is mine.
Half of your half is mine. Vow amended.
At that moment, Yeoni's phone rang. Not an unknown number. The screen showed a name they hadn't been able to delete in three years.
[ Incoming · Customer Support: Universe ]
Now? During the wedding?
Answer. After all that waiting, another delay might hurt its feelings.
Congratulations, valued customer. Destiny Customer Support, the universe speaking. We're calling with your resolution notice and a satisfaction survey.
Right now? After not calling once in three years?
Yes. Today is when the outcome becomes final. Case received: spring when you were twenty-three. Case completed: today.
If you were satisfied with the process, please leave a star rating. Your valued review will greatly help our next customer.

Yeoni looked at the guests. Seo Hanbi blowing her nose into a handkerchief. Saebyeok hiding behind his script. Moka still rapping through the phone. Byeongha beneath the umbrella, one shoulder half wet.
At first, even half a star felt too generous.
Their thumb moved over the stars. One, two, three, four. Then five.
[ ★★★★★ · Review: Almost took one off for being late, but didn't. Worst wait time. Friendly agent. Satisfied with the result. Would not buy again. Once was enough. ]
Thank you for your valued review. Have an ordinary spring.
The call ended. The rain stopped. Sunlight poured between the clouds. Wet cherry petals fell, glittering.
Was that the universe? The universe calls weddings?
Should have put it on the guest list. Though it probably wouldn't give a wedding gift.
It would charge a consultation fee. Three years' worth.
What did you write?
Secret. I said I'd rate you again every year. I'll show you next year.
A white cat passed their feet. Park Byeongha sneezed. The guests laughed. Yeoni laughed too.
The bouquet left Yeoni's hand and landed precisely in Seo Hanbi's arms. Startled, she dropped her umbrella. Saebyeok applauded. No one lent the applause, and no one collected it.
Am I allowed to accept this?
You absolutely accept that. Don't repay it.
Ordinary. A truly ordinary spring.
That's enough. Next spring too. And the spring after.
[ Destiny restored · A Spring in Reality ]
